text:
maya: heads up — in us-east1 we're seeing a pile of gpu pods pending but a few racks are at 90% while others have free GPUs. looks like scheduler is shadowing onto two racks and not balancing. noticed this after yesterday's rack label rollout. anyone else?
aj: saw that too. stack: a dozen model workers pending, same nodeSelector: gpu=true, but node distribution is odd. maybe labels applied unevenly during rollout.
liam: can you paste the kubectl output? also did the deploy bot change any topologySpreadConstraints?
maya: paste below
```
# kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending
model-worker-abc   Pending   0/1   <none>   20m   10.0.1.45   us-east1-rack-a
model-worker-def   Pending   0/1   <none>   18m   10.0.1.46   us-east1-rack-a
... (lots on rack-a)
```
nina: quick hypothesis: some nodes in rack-b lost the label gpu=true during the label rollout, so scheduler thinks only rack-a is valid. or there's an extra taint on the others.
carter: checked node labels earlier — i saw a few nodes with label gpu=legacy instead of gpu=true. that would make the nodeSelector mismatch.
aj: also found a recent scheduler config change that added a topology weight favoring rack-local for performance. combined with mislabels that's amplifying packing.
liam: ok two issues: mislabels + topology bias. short-term mitigation: we can temporarily remove the topology weight, or patch the nodeSelector in the deployment to be more permissive (not ideal). better: fix node labels then let scheduler rebalance.
maya: what's the fastest safe fix? we have 30% increased latency in affected routes.
carter: fastest safe is to correct the labels on the nodes and trigger descheduler to evict mis-placed pods. command:
```
kubectl label node node-12 gpu=true --overwrite
kubectl label node node-13 gpu=true --overwrite
# then trigger descheduler job
kubectl create job desched-fix --from=cronjob/descheduler -n infra
```
nina: we should also roll back the topology weight in scheduler config to avoid further grouping while nodes heal. that's a 1-line change in configmap: scheduler-config.yaml weightTopology: 100 -> 0
aj: agree. i'll prepare a quick canary: rollback weight in us-east1 only, watch the distribution for 10 minutes.
liam: also add a short-term admission hook to reject pods with nodeSelector gpu=legacy so we don't keep scheduling to wrong nodes, and add a job to find nodes with unexpected labels. I'll send a one-off script.
maya: thanks. can someone open a ticket and own the end-to-end? includes label fix, rollback, descheduler run, and postmortem.
aj: created INF-9999: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9999 — assigned to carter, due EOD.
carter: ack. doing labels now, will post status in 10m. @sre-bot can you enqueue an alert suppress for the noisy PodPending alert for 30m?
sre-bot: Alert suppression scheduled: PodPending-high (30m) — reason: remediation in progress by carter. :white_check_mark:
maya: nice. once labels are fixed and descheduler runs, let's check costs — we've got bursty over-provision on rack-a. might need to rebalance autoscaler settings to prevent wasted preemptible capacity.
liam: noted — will follow up with a quick autoscaler tweak suggestion in INF-9999. also we should add a check in the rollout job to verify node labels after label changes.
carter: update: labeled 6 nodes, starting descheduler job now.
carter: descheduler job finished, seeing evictions => pods redistributed to rack-b. distribution looks normalized (~40/60 split).
maya: verified in-app — latency back to baseline. thanks all. will keep INF-9999 open for postmortem and a small CI gate for label rollouts.
aj: +1 :thumbsup:
nina: great job. learned lesson: rollout gating and label verification are cheap and effective.
carter: closing remark: let's add automation to auto-relabel legacy->true in next infra sprint to avoid human misses.
maya: agreed, assign to eng-platform roadmap. thanks team.
